keys.default: (chart's global.tolerations, JSON — the runtime's own tolerations)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON array of toleration objects stamped onto every SPAWNED Pod's spec so a bare `kubectl run` bot/agent Pod (not a Deployment child) tolerates the same taints the runtime does — else it strands Pending forever on an all-tainted pool (#673). Empty [] ⇒ no tolerations; malformed JSON is fatal at spawn (a silently dropped constraint is the bug)

keys.default: (chart's global.nodeSelector, JSON — the runtime's own nodeSelector)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON object of node-label selectors stamped onto every SPAWNED Pod's spec so a bare `kubectl run` bot/agent Pod schedules onto the same pool the runtime does. Empty {} ⇒ no selector; malformed JSON is fatal at spawn (#673)

keys.default: (unset — the meeting-bot class declares no cpu, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: CPU cores every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod declares. runtime.v1 carries one value per dimension, so it sets BOTH the container's request and its limit (Guaranteed QoS) — the declaration a namespace ResourceQuota admits on (#1005). Unset/empty ⇒ no cpu declared (the pre-#1005 unbounded spawn); a non-numeric value is fatal at boot

keys.default: (unset — the meeting-bot class declares no memory, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: memory (MiB) every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod declares, as BOTH request and limit. A HARD ceiling — a bot exceeding it is OOM-killed mid-meeting — so size it for real meetings, not for the smallest node. Unset/empty ⇒ no memory declared; a non-numeric value is fatal at boot (#1005)

keys.default: (unset — the agent-worker class declares no cpu, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: CPU cores every SPAWNED agent-worker Pod declares, as BOTH request and limit. Sized INDEPENDENTLY of the meeting bot — a code harness is not a browser — so an operator can right-size each class alone (#1005). Unset/empty ⇒ no cpu declared; a non-numeric value is fatal at boot

keys.default: (unset — the agent-worker class declares no memory, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: memory (MiB) every SPAWNED agent-worker Pod declares, as BOTH request and limit. Unset/empty ⇒ no memory declared; a non-numeric value is fatal at boot (#1005)

DOCKER-HOST path (NOT an in-container path) to a claude credentials JSON (~/.claude/.credentials.json); the docker backend bind-mounts it READ-ONLY into every spawned agent-worker at /root/.claude/.credentials.json — the claude-code runner's subscription credential path. compose also mirror-mounts it into the runtime container at /var/lib/vexa/host-claude-credentials so the config.v1 file probe can verify the host file actually exists (docker turns a MISSING host path into an empty directory in the worker → 'Model inference failed: Not logged in'). PAIR IT WITH HOST_CLAUDE_DIR: this single-FILE mirror is pinned to the inode it was created with, so it goes stale the moment the CLI refreshes the token

keys.default: (unset — only the legacy single-file mirror is available)
keys.description: DOCKER-HOST path of the claude config DIRECTORY (~/.claude), mirror-mounted READ-ONLY into the long-lived runtime + agent-api containers at /var/lib/vexa/host-claude. Same credential as HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS, delivered in the shape that SURVIVES A TOKEN REFRESH: the CLI replaces .credentials.json via rename(2) (a NEW inode), and a single-FILE bind stays pinned to the inode it was created with, so a long-lived container reads the pre-refresh token until it is recreated (32h of 'Not logged in' on the dogfood stack, 2026-08-31). A DIRECTORY bind resolves the filename live. Set it to the parent of HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS
DOCKER-HOST path to Codex subscription auth (~/.codex/auth.json); mounted read-only into spawned codex-runner workers at /root/.codex/auth.json
